subject: Order Form redlines: SLA & support windows
messages:
From: Ariel Stone <ariel.stone@helixai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-07T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal order form + SLA clarifications

Mina / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft order form — attached are our redlines (Helix_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf). A few SLA items we'd like to resolve before routing to procurement/legal on our side:

- Uptime: we proposed 99.9% availability and want to confirm Redwood's standard for availability commitments on Dedicated plans.
- Service credits: our procurement team expects credits to accrue per calendar month and stack for repeated failures; proposed credit = (monthly fee) * (percentage below target).
- Response times: we need a firm P1 acknowledgement and P1 resolution SLA (we suggested 30m ack, 4h resolution).
- Maintenance windows: Can you confirm max monthly planned maintenance and advance notice (we asked for <= 6 hours/month, 72h notice)?

We also included some specific language around emergency maintenance carve-outs and a cap on cumulative credits. Please let us know Redwood's position so we can finalize internally and circulate to our legal.

Attachments: Helix_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf

Best,
Ariel Stone
Head of Procurement, HelixAI
ariel.stone@helixai.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Stone <ariel.stone@helixai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-07T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal order form + SLA clarifications

Ariel — thanks for the redlines and the clear list. I uploaded an internal working sheet (SLA_matrix_v2.xlsx) with our suggested compromise positions and marked items we want legal to own. Summary of our preferred positions below: 

- Uptime: Redwood can accept 99.95% for the Dedicated tier you indicated. We consider 99.95% a baseline for committed capacity; 99.9% would be for a lower-priced tier.
- Service credits: we propose a tiered credit table (attached sheet) with a monthly cap equal to 100% of the monthly invoice (we cannot offer unlimited stacking). Credits apply pro rata by affected region/route.
- Response times: we can commit to a 30m P1 acknowledgement and a 2h P1 response window for critical incidents during business hours; 4h response during agreed support hours for weekends. For 24x7 coverage and <30m resolution targets we need a higher support tier.
- Maintenance windows: Planned maintenance limited to 4 hours/month by default, with 48h notice for non-emergency work. Emergency maintenance (security or critical reliability fixes) is excluded but we'll notify as soon as possible.

Next steps: Marissa — can you review the attached matrix and draft counter-language for the order form & MSA? Jonas, can you confirm the proposed maintenance cap is operationally feasible (we may need a staggered approach across regions).

I'll set up a short call with Ariel and procurement next week to triage open items.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-08T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Renewal order form + SLA clarifications

Team — quick legal/risks note after reading Ariel's redlines and Mina's matrix. Key asks for our counterproposal (redlines_v2.docx attached):

1) Uptime definition: Insist on explicit measurement methodology (per-region hourly samples, exclusion of scheduled maintenance windows, exclusion of force majeure). We should avoid vague "service interruption" language.

2) Credits: Cap credits to 100% monthly invoice and add annual aggregate cap (e.g., cannot exceed 3x monthly invoice within a rolling 12-month period). This protects against repeated outlier months.

3) Maintenance carve-outs: Accept 4 hours/month planned maintenance by default, but require our right to cluster maintenance during low-traffic windows and to use a monthly blackout limit (i.e., we will not be liable for credits for scheduled maintenance provided we give 48h notice and keep planned downtime to <= 6 hours in a single calendar month).

4) Response SLAs: Push back on deterministic "resolution" times. We can commit to acknowledgment/triage SLAs and target resolution windows for defined categories, with an escalation matrix and target MTTRs rather than hard contractual resolution commitments for complex infra issues.

5) Escalation/handoffs: Add a routed escalation path (SRE on-call -> Account Engineering -> VP Ops) with contact points and optional weekly incident reviews for the first 90 days post cutover.

Action items: Mina, propose the language changes from redlines_v2.docx into the order form. Jonas/Aditya: please confirm maintenance/rollout constraints operationally. Once we have that, we'll push a tracked-change counter to Ariel and Helix legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ariel Stone <ariel.stone@helixai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-09T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal order form + SLA clarifications

Thanks, Mina and Marissa — helpful. A few follow-ups from Helix procurement/legal after internal review: 

- Helix can accept 99.95% as long as the measurement/region carve-outs are explicit and the credits are applied per-affected region.
- We understand Redwood's need for a credit cap, but can you soften the annual aggregate cap? Our ask is a 2x rolling 12-month cap rather than 3x.
- Response SLAs: Helix is asking for guaranteed P1 acknowledgement within 30m and a P1 target "time to mitigation" of 2 hours in practice (we realize full resolution may take longer). Is Redwood willing to add a "time to mitigation" clause (measurable steps taken to restore customer-facing traffic) as a commitment?
- Maintenance: 48h notice is acceptable, but can we request a maximum of 4h/month for planned maintenance (not 6h).

Quoted for context: "On 2024-11-08 Mina wrote: 'Planned maintenance limited to 4 hours/month by default, with 48h notice for non-emergency work.'"

If the above points are acceptable, we'll ask our legal to review the tracked counter and proceed to DocuSign. We'll also want the SRE escalation contacts (names/phone) to be included in the appendix before signature.

Ariel

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Stone <ariel.stone@helixai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-12T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Finalize: Order Form SLA redlines and sign-off path

Ariel — thanks for the quick turnaround and flexibility. Confirming what we'll put in the counter (tracking & doc to follow):

- Uptime: 99.95% availability, measured per-region with explicit sampling methodology and exclusion for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- Credits: Tiered monthly credits per SLA matrix, with a monthly cap = 100% of monthly invoice and a rolling 12-month cap = 2x monthly invoice (compromise from our original ask).
- Response: 30m P1 acknowledgement + target 2h time-to-mitigation for P1 incidents; full resolution language will be operational/targeted rather than absolute in the MSA. We'll add the escalation matrix (SRE on-call -> Account Engineering -> VP Ops) to the appendix.
- Maintenance: Planned maintenance default to 4 hours/month with 48h notice; emergency maintenance excluded with best-effort notice. We'll include language about low-traffic scheduling and regional staggering to minimize customer impact.

Attachments we will circulate with tracked changes: legal_redlines_v2.docx, SLA_matrix_v2.xlsx. Once legal review is complete on your side, we'll send a DocuSign packet for the Order Form and MSA merge (DocuSign link will be provided; draft link: https://www.docusign.net/sign/12345abcdef).

Next steps: 
1) Marissa to finalize tracked-change counter and route to Ariel's counsel by end of day 11/13.
2) Jonas & Aditya to provide SRE on-call names/phones and confirm operational feasibility for staggered maintenance by 11/14.
3) Ariel to confirm Helix legal's availability for a 30-minute sign-off call the week of 11/18 if needed.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
